title: Income Inequality and Status Seeking: Searching for Positional Goods in Unequal U.S. States

selection.evidence: Assigned by mark as item 5 of 8 in a blinded known-answer control of my reading protocol (identifiers only, 2026-10-23T16:11). No prior knowledge of the paper; prior suspicion: none.

cost.compute_notes: Full text NOT reachable: not OA; WRAP record has no file; SAGE Cloudflare; Wayback holds paywall wrappers (web.archive.org/web/20210310063629/...doi/pdf/...). Read: PubMed abstract + the authors' OSF reproduction instructions. OSF fitgz (parent holds no files; 4 components) acquired with checksums and analysed in Python.

triggers: income inequality status seeking google searches
defunct service makes a pipeline irreproducible
known-answer control psychological science 2015 open data

claims.statement: Of the 40 search terms used more frequently in states with greater residual income inequality (Gini net of income, population, urbanisation and foreign-born share), more than 70% were classified as status goods; of the 40 used more frequently in less unequal states, 0%.
claims.scope: 50 US states (DC omitted), Google Correlate top-40 positive and top-40 negative terms, 60 MTurk raters per term.

quantities.name: status_terms_outside_three_query_families
quantities.baseline: of 29 status-classified terms; families: Ralph Lauren 6, David Yurman 8, loafers 3

our_assessment.why: Abstract-only read. The deposit reproduces the headline proportions (29/40 vs 0/40 under a majority rule) and the residuals exactly. Not assessable without the paper: rater blinding, the test used, robustness. Counts are inflated by near-duplicate query families.

claims.statement: Residual-based analysis offers a methodology for using Google Correlate 'while avoiding confounds and high risks of spurious correlations' (abstract).

quantities.name: residual_inequality_R2_on_census_region
quantities.baseline: p < .0001; top residual states CT, LA, NY, MA, MS, AL, TN, RI

our_assessment.why: Abstract-only read. On the deposit, 40% of the residual is Census region: the measure carries the Northeast/Deep-South geography the four controls do not remove, and the status terms read as a regional preppy idiom. The confound the residual avoids is income, not culture. Google Correlate was shut down in 2019, so the selection step cannot be re-run by anyone.

checked.how: Read tool on the PDF (2 pages)
checked.result: Step-by-step census downloads via factfinder.census.gov (retired by the Census Bureau in 2020) and Google Correlate (shut down 2019). The steps are documented; the services are gone.

artifacts.locator: https://osf.io/tqi83/ Inequality_Control_Data.xlsx and https://osf.io/437xf/ open_access_residuals.xlsx (50 states)
artifacts.fetch_cmd: for g in tqi83 437xf xfmbq tkfxd; do python dev-science-ops/paper-retrospective-reproducibility/tools/acquire.py https://osf.io/$g/ --out "$(python zoo-knowledge-base/tools/assets.py path paper-downloads/walasek2015-income-inequality-status-seeking)/osf_$g"; done

checked.result: OLS GINIindex ~ log_mean_inc + Population + percurban + PercentForeignBorn reproduces the deposited residuals to 5e-6 (R2 = .342). Population enters raw.

artifacts.locator: https://osf.io/xfmbq/ RatingData.xlsx (80 terms x yes/no/don't know counts, correlation r)

checked.result: 60 raters per term. Negative r stored as text with a typographic minus. Correlations .73-.78 (positive) and -.68 to -.72 (negative): the top of a search over the Google Correlate database, not estimates of association strength.
The step that selected the 80 terms cannot be re-run; its output survives only as the term list in a3.

relations.why: Item 5 of mark's blinded known-answer control of the reading protocol (abstract-only: full text unreachable).

open_questions: Full text needed (mark asked 2026-10-25: send PDF, swap reserve, or score as abstract-only). Were raters blind to the source list? Was region or culture considered?

Does the status/non-status asymmetry survive a regional control? With Google Correlate gone, the testable version is Google Trends state-level interest for the 29 status terms regressed on residual Gini plus Census-region dummies.
